name: Microsoft Azure AI Speech (text to speech)
positioning: Microsoft's Speech service in Azure Foundry Tools, providing neural and HD text-to-speech voices in 100+ languages and locales with SSML, custom and personal voice options, and REST and WebSocket access.

pricing.model: Per character synthesized, billed per 1M characters, with a free F0 tier, a pay-as-you-go S0 tier and discounted commitment tiers. The pricing page renders prices client-side, so figures below come from the Azure Retail Prices API (eastus, USD).
pricing.headline: Neural voices $15 per 1M characters; Neural HD $22 per 1M characters (eastus retail list).

tiers.name: Neural
tiers.notes: Meter 'S1 Neural Text To Speech Characters'. Azure's page groups 'Neural/Neural HD Flash' on one price line; the mapping of this meter to that line is inferred.

tiers.name: Neural HD
tiers.notes: Meter 'Neural HD Text to Speech Characters', effective 2026-03-01.

tiers.name: Personal Voice synthesis
tiers.notes: Voice creation listed as free on the pricing page; voice profile storage billed separately.

tiers.name: Custom (Professional) voice, real-time
tiers.notes: Meter 'S1 Custom Neural Realtime Characters'; training and endpoint hosting billed separately (hosting $4.032 per model-hour per retail meter). Custom voice is a limited-access feature.

tiers.name: Long audio (batch)
tiers.notes: Meters 'S1 Neural Long Audio Characters' and custom equivalent.

tiers.name: Commitment tiers (Neural)
tiers.unit: USD per month plus overage per 1M characters
tiers.notes: For example 80M tier $960 per month with overage $12.00 per 1M; 400M tier $3,900 per month with overage $9.75; 2000M tier $15,000 with overage $7.50; 4000M tier $24,000 with overage $6.00 (retail API, Azure-connected).

tiers.name: MAI-Voice
tiers.notes: Listed on the pricing page; price not available in the retail API query.

pricing.freeTier: Free (F0): Neural text to speech 0.5 million characters per month (pricing page); F0 rate limit 20 transactions per 60 seconds.

voices.languages: 100+ languages and locales for standard (neural) voices
voices.customVoiceOrCloning: Professional voice fine-tuning requires a recorded consent statement from the voice talent; custom voice is a limited-access feature per the pricing page. Personal voice is also offered ($24 per 1M characters synthesis; voice creation free).

compatibility.note: REST text-to-speech takes SSML (Content-Type application/ssml+xml) posted to the resource's cognitiveservices endpoint with an X-Microsoft-OutputFormat header and subscription key or bearer token. Azure OpenAI neural voices are also selectable within the Speech service per the overview page, but no OpenAI-style speech route on the Speech service was read.

licensing.attributionOrConditions: Custom voices require voice-talent consent and are limited access.

limits.perRequestCharacters: Audio length per request up to 10 minutes (longer is truncated); up to 50 distinct voice and audio tags in SSML; SSML message up to 64 KB per WebSocket turn
limits.concurrency: Real-time TTS: F0 20 transactions per 60 seconds (not adjustable); S0 30 transactions per second default, adjustable up to 1,000 TPS.

compliance.note: No compliance certification statements were found on the speech pages read; the text-to-speech data, privacy and security page defines GDPR terms but is not a compliance claim. Microsoft publishes compliance material at platform level that was not reviewed.

strengths.claim: Very broad language coverage: standard neural voices in 100+ languages and locales.
Both REST and WebSocket synthesis, many output formats including 48 kHz and telephony mu-law and A-law.
Custom professional voice and personal voice options with consent requirements, plus Neural HD voices.
Commitment tiers lower the effective per-character rate at volume (for example overage $6.00 per 1M on the 4000M tier).
Free F0 tier with 0.5 million Neural characters per month.

limitations.claim: Neural HD voices, personal voices and embedded voices do not support all SSML tags.
Custom voice is a limited-access feature.
Microsoft documents that most HTTP 429 errors with standard voices stem from limited backend capacity for a specific voice in the selected region rather than quota.

stepsToMove: Endpoint: Azure takes SSML (<speak><voice name='en-US-...Neural'>...) in a POST to the regional Speech resource with X-Microsoft-OutputFormat; ReadAloud takes the OpenAI speech request or the ElevenLabs route with plain input text.
Auth: Azure uses a subscription key or token for a regional resource; ReadAloud uses an API key.
Voice names: Azure voice names (for example en-US-ChristopherNeural) do not exist on ReadAloud; choose a ReadAloud voice id.
SSML: strip or translate SSML (prosody, styles, voice tags); check ReadAloud's documented SSML behavior.
Output formats: X-Microsoft-OutputFormat values like riff-24khz-16bit-mono-pcm or audio-24khz-96kbitrate-mono-mp3 map to ReadAloud response_format or output_format; confirm supported subset.
WebSocket: Azure's SDK streams over WebSocket; ReadAloud's WebSocket route has its own message protocol.

bestFor: Organizations on Azure or Microsoft 365 that need enterprise commitment tiers, many locales, and custom or personal voice options within the same cloud contract.
